question: On 30 and 31 July 2026, the city of Ceuta in Spain experienced a massive influx of migrants from neighbouring Morocco. At least 80 000 people illegally crossed the border of a Member State, in a movement that can only be described as an invasion. To prevent such events from recurring, closer monitoring of this border – which is clearly a sensitive one – is required.

Frontex is able to request satellite surveillance of an area or to obtain satellite imagery of it. Footage from previous surveillance operations may also be available. Consulting these images could help to explain the sequence of events in greater detail and is therefore essential for the surveillance of the EU’s common borders.
Furthermore, rumours of a second wave of migrants due to arrive around 15 August 2026 will surely have prompted increased monitoring. 1.

Can the Commission state whether Frontex, at the request of the Spanish Government, obtained satellite imagery prior to the migrant influx that might have helped to prevent it or in anticipation of a possible population movement around 15 August 2026?
If Frontex did not, did it obtain the images retrospectively in order to analyse the events and understand the causes of this crisis?
If such images exist, when and how will Members of the European Parliament be able to access them?
